name: Relay

description.project: A webhook delivery service that accepts events, sends them to registered endpoints, and provides delivery history for debugging failed integrations.
description.technical: Backend service built with Go and PostgreSQL. Uses Redis-backed queues to schedule delivery attempts, HTTP workers to dispatch webhook requests, and exponential backoff to retry transient failures.

features.name: Endpoint registration
features.description: Users can register webhook destinations and configure which event types should be delivered to each endpoint.
features.implementation: Created endpoint and subscription records in PostgreSQL, with API handlers for registration and updates. Validated destination URLs and event selections before persisting configuration.

features.name: Asynchronous delivery queue
features.description: Accepted events are queued and delivered asynchronously so event producers do not wait for destination servers.
features.implementation: Persisted delivery jobs and used Redis-backed workers to claim pending work, execute outbound HTTP requests, and record response status and timing information.

features.name: Retry handling
features.description: Temporary delivery failures are retried automatically, with attempts visible in the delivery history.
features.implementation: Classified delivery outcomes and scheduled retryable failures using exponential backoff. Recorded each attempt separately so users can inspect response codes, timestamps, and the final delivery state.

highlights: Implemented asynchronous webhook dispatch using Redis-backed workers.
Added retry scheduling with exponential backoff for transient failures.
Stored per-attempt delivery history for integration debugging.
